transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, thanks for seeing me. I guess I'm here because... most days I wake up and it already feels like there's this heavy, gray weight sitting on me. And it just doesn't lift. Even when I'm out working with the landscaping crew, or at home around my kids, I just can't shake it. It's this constant low, hollow feeling... like I'm just going through the motions every single day.
Has this heavy, gray feeling you're describing been going on continuously, or have you had periods in the past where you felt better for a while before it came back?

It's been continuous. I haven't really had any breaks from it, to be honest. 

I've been feeling this way for... well, it's been about three years and three months now. It started right around the time the groundskeeping contract changed our schedule at work. The longer days just kind of took over my life, and that heavy feeling settled in. It just hasn't let up since then.
During these past three years, have there been any stretches of time—even a few weeks or a couple of months—where the heavy feeling lifted and you felt more like your normal self?

No, not really. I mean... I can't think of a single time where it just went away for a few weeks or anything. There haven't been any stretches like that where I felt normal again. It's just been there every single day, without a break.
Before these three years started, did you ever have periods in your life—maybe weeks or months—where you felt depressed or down like this?

No, not before this started. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, but nothing like this. Before those three years, I felt fine. I went to work, came home, lived my life... I didn't have any long stretches where I felt down or heavy like I do now. It really just started when that schedule changed and never left.

During these past three years, have there been any stretches of time—even just a couple of months—where you felt noticeably better, with fewer of these heavy feelings, even if you weren't back to your old self completely?
No, honestly, I haven't. Like I said, it's just been a constant thing. There hasn't been a month, or even a couple of weeks, where it felt lighter. It's just the same heavy feeling every day.

During these three years of feeling this heavy weight, have there been any times when things got significantly worse—like where you couldn't sleep or slept way too much, your appetite changed a lot, you couldn't concentrate on anything, or you had thoughts about harming yourself?

No, not really. It hasn't spiked or gotten drastically worse like that. I mean, my sleep is always a bit off, and I don't always feel like eating, but it's just a steady, heavy feeling. It hasn't dropped off a cliff into something worse where I couldn't function at all or had thoughts about hurting myself. It's just... the same weight, day in and day out.

During these three years, or even before that, have you ever had periods where your mood was the opposite—where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep but still felt great, or felt like you could do a lot more than usual?

No, I haven't ever had anything like that. I've never been the type to run on no sleep or feel super energetic. Even before all this started, I was just a regular guy going to work and coming home. I've never had a time where I felt wired or anything like what you're describing.
Have there ever been times when you felt like you were accomplishing a lot, talking more than usual, or your thoughts were moving faster than normal—even if you didn't feel energetic or wired?

No, nothing like that. I've never been a big talker, and my mind doesn't really race or anything. I just... I just go to work, do my landscaping, and come home. There's never been a time where I felt like I was getting a ton done or thinking faster than normal. It's always just been pretty slow and heavy.

Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually confident, took on new projects or ideas impulsively, or felt like you were more creative or productive than your normal baseline—even if it wasn't accompanied by high energy?

No, nothing like that. I'm not really a... a creative guy to begin with. I just do my job. I've never had a time where I felt super confident or started taking on a bunch of new projects out of nowhere. I just stick to my normal routine. I don't really do anything impulsive.
Have you ever had a period where you needed significantly less sleep than usual—like feeling well-rested after only 3 or 4 hours of sleep—and you felt fine or good during the day, not tired?

No, never. If I only get three or four hours of sleep, I feel awful the next day. I've never had a time where I felt fine or well-rested running on that little sleep, especially doing physical work all day. I'm just... I'm usually just tired, to be honest.

Have you ever had a time when you felt really good about yourself, like you could do things better than other people, or felt like you had special abilities or talents—even if you weren't particularly energetic?

No, I can't say I have. I don't have any special talents or... or abilities. I'm just a regular guy doing yard work. I definitely don't walk around thinking I'm better at things than other people. Honestly, most days I feel like I'm just barely getting by, not... not feeling good about myself like that.

Have you ever had a period, even just a few weeks, where you felt noticeably happier or more optimistic than you do now, and during that time you were able to get things done more easily or felt motivated to do things—even if you weren't necessarily feeling energetic or wired?

No... no, I haven't. I don't really remember the last time I felt optimistic about anything. I definitely haven't had a couple of weeks where things felt easy or I was highly motivated. It's pretty much just been a struggle to get through the day's work for a long, long time now.
